text: Preface

title: The Alan Machine
text:
How to read this book
This book is about a machine that does not exist. We call it Alan, and we use it to ask a question physics takes very seriously: can entropy be reversed, and if it could, what would happen to time?
You do not need a physics degree to read it. The chapters are written for anyone who is curious. When the math helps, it shows up in boxes marked Going deeper, which you can open or skip. The story works either way.
Some chapters have a companion paper, written for specialists, with the full argument. You will find the papers in the last part of the book, and each chapter tells you when one exists.
Along the way, we keep three kinds of statement apart. Unmarked claims are established physics, with references you can check. Boxes marked Extrapolation follow from established physics, but only if their stated assumptions hold. Boxes marked Speculation hold ideas that are conceivable but that no evidence supports yet. A thought experiment is only useful if you always know which of the three you are reading.

title: About the Papers
text:
The chapters tell the story. The papers make the argument.
Some chapters have a companion paper with the full scientific treatment of their subject: the derivations, the assumptions and the references a specialist would expect. Each paper stands on its own, with its own authors, abstract and references, and can be cited independently of the book. A chapter can lean on several papers, and a paper can support several chapters.
